title: Memory ↔ Consciousness — Scale, Timeline, and Theory Matrix
content_html:
Memory ↔ Consciousness — Theory Matrix

Memory arises early as adaptive state; consciousness likely emerges gradually with integration, temporal continuity, and global accessibility.

Single Cell: Adaptive States without Experience

Habituation, chemotaxis, molecular memory; no evidence of subjective experience.

  • Slime mold route optimization
  • Paramecium habituation

Invertebrate: Associative Learning

Plasticity enables conditioning; procedural memory dominates.

  • Aplysia gill-withdrawal conditioning
  • Insect associative learning (bees)

Vertebrate : Integration & Spatial Memory

Hippocampal-like structures; place cells; replay; flexible navigation.

  • Teleost pallium spatial tasks
  • Rodent replay during rest/sleep

Mammal/Bird: Episodic-like Memory & Metacognition

What–where–when memory; planning and confidence reports in some species.

  • Scrub jays recall cache content & timing
  • Corvids/parrots planning; primate metacognition

Human: Autobiography & Global Access

Narrative self, language, theory of mind; global broadcasting across systems.

  • Scene construction & imagination
  • Verbal report

Consciousness Theories vs. Scale

Theory Single-cell Invertebrate Vertebrate Mammal/Bird Human Predicted Threshold
Global Workspace (GWT)
— global access, long-range broadcasting		 — — △ ✓ ✓ Mammal/Bird (developed long-range networks)
Recurrent Processing (RPT)
— local recurrent loops suffice		 — △ ✓ ✓ ✓ Vertebrate (with robust recurrent circuits)
Integrated Information (IIT)
— graded by Φ (integration)		 • △ ✓ ✓ ✓ Continuum (non-zero Φ even in simple systems)

Symbols: ✓ predicted present; △ possible/limited; • minimal; — not predicted.

Evidence Snapshot by Level

Level Key Findings Representative Sources
Single-cell Slime molds solve mazes; habituation in non-neural organisms. Nakagaki et al., 2000; Boisseau et al., 2016.
Invertebrate Associative learning; identified synaptic plasticity. Kandel, 2001; Glanzman, 2010.
Vertebrate Place/grid cells; hippocampal replay; spatial cognition in fish/rodents. O’Keefe & Nadel, 1978; Buzsáki, 2015; Broglio et al., 2003.
Mammal/Bird Episodic-like memory; planning; metacognition in some species. Clayton & Dickinson, 1998; Raby et al., 2007; Smith et al., 2003.
Human Global workspace; scene construction; autobiographical recollection. Dehaene & Changeux, 2011; Hassabis & Maguire, 2007; Tulving, 2002.
